status: seed: concept, stills and motion prompts approved 2026-10-26. Posts as episode 030. Test render of clips 1 and 4 first.
title_hook: Pressure gets answers. Not the person.
concept: A bright, quiet house of white plaster in flat morning daylight. A pale oak door swings open toward camera and the corridor behind it stretches away instead of coming closer. Every door opened leads to another identical tidy room: one chair, one empty cup, one blank frame. The person who lives here is never seen. The only signs of them are a shadow passing under a closed door and a curtain moving in a room the camera never reaches. The camera stops pushing and waits. The film returns to the first door.
theme: Answers given under pressure are not trust freely given.
quote: Pressure can get you answers. Only trust gets you the person.
core_metaphor: A house that answers every knock with another polite empty room. The person who lives there is real, but never in the room you pushed your way into.
emotional_arc: a familiar frustration -> a paradox you can see -> the tidy rooms are for visitors -> answers are not trust -> what kind of presence earns a door
recurring_element: one canonical doorway: a tall pale oak door with a small brass (#C6A94F) latch, set in a pale plaster wall; behind each doorway an identical tidy room of white plaster with one plain wooden chair, one empty white cup on a small table and one blank white framed picture
material: Bone-white (#F5F2EB) plaster walls, pale oak doors, small brass (#C6A94F) latches, light oak floorboards. Flat, soft overcast morning daylight from tall windows on the left; no lamps, no warm glow, no dark rooms. Shadows are soft and grey.

sound_event.prompt: Close-miked brass door latch lifting and a light oak door swinging open in a quiet bright house: crisp latch click, soft hinge, a breath of air, faint birdsong outside a window. Dry and realistic. No music, no impacts, no whooshes.

primary_prompt: A restrained photorealistic 9:16 film about a house that never lets its owner be found. One bright house of bone-white (#F5F2EB) plaster in soft overcast morning daylight: pale oak doors with small brass (#C6A94F) latches open onto identical tidy rooms, each with one wooden chair, one empty white cup and one blank white frame. The person who lives there is never shown; only a shadow or a moving curtain hints at them. The architecture stays legible and consistent. Slow, physically credible camera, real daylight. No faces, no figures, no darkness, no warm glow, no readable text, no lens flares.

hook.text: You asked again. They answered again. Somehow you know them less.
hook.visual: A door opening toward camera onto a long white corridor. Already swinging on the first frame: a tall pale oak door with a small brass (#C6A94F) latch opens toward the lens, bright overcast daylight. Through the widening gap, a long white plaster corridor runs to another closed oak door at its far end. Motion: the door keeps swinging slowly open while the camera advances gently toward the doorway with a smooth, restrained forward dolly; natural perspective deepens. One dominant subject, clean bright contrast, readable at phone size. One continuous shot. No people, no lettering, no lens flares.

build.text: Every answer opens another door. Past it, a tidy room. One chair. One empty cup. Nothing of them. The person you came for is always one room away.
build.visual: A tidy room made for visitors, not for living. Slow forward track through a small bone-white (#F5F2EB) plaster room in soft daylight: one plain wooden chair, one empty white cup on a small table, one blank white framed picture, everything neat and untouched. In the far wall, another pale oak door with a brass (#C6A94F) latch stands slightly open onto more white wall. The camera keeps moving toward it at one steady pace. No people, no readable text, no clutter.

pivot.text: Pressure can get you answers. Only trust gets you the person.
pivot.visual: The same empty seat repeated down one long corridor. A long white plaster (#F5F2EB) corridor with light oak herringbone floors in soft overcast daylight: the same small wooden table with one empty white cup and the same wooden chair repeat in a line down the left side, pale doors line the right, and at the far end, dead centre, one closed door. Symmetrical, clean. Motion: slow, steady push forward down the corridor; the closed far door never seems to get closer. The corridor keeps its exact geometry. No people, no readable text, no glow.

resolution.text: An invitation is not yours to manufacture. Be someone a closed door is safe around.
resolution.visual: A closed door with someone standing behind it. Front-on at standing height, a closed panelled door in pale warm beige with a small brass (#C6A94F) lever latch, set in a bone-white (#F5F2EB) plaster wall above light oak herringbone floorboards, soft overcast daylight from the left, a thin line of daylight under the door. Motion: locked camera; the door stays fully shut and the latch never moves; a soft shadow slides slowly into the line of light under the door and stops in the middle, as someone on the other side steps close and stands still. No people visible, no readable text.

mobius_close.text: Because the next time you ask...
mobius_close.visual: Clip 1's first seconds played in reverse: the door swings slowly back toward its starting position and the camera eases back, so the last frame is exactly the first frame of the reel. No people, no lettering.

transitions.how: Accelerate the push through the open doorway in the last 0.6 s of clip 1 and dissolve into the tidy room already tracking forward.
Cut exactly on the first syllable of 'Pressure' from the ground-level track to the overhead grid; the jump in point of view is the point.
A soft cloud shadow crosses the grid of rooms at the end of clip 3 and lifts off the closed door in clip 4; the brass latch catches the returning daylight.
In the last 0.5 s of clip 4 the camera eases toward the latch and dissolves onto the first door's latch, already lifting.
The close is clip 1 reversed, so its last frame is the reel's first frame; the loop has no fade or transition of its own.

distinct_from.how: PRESENCE is about seeing someone daily and misreading them, shown with a face, a figure, a dark stone hall and a revealed warm interior. RECEPTION is about pushing for answers and getting a front room, shown in a bright daylight house with no people at all, and the hidden life is never revealed. No shared imagery (no faces, black stone, gold light or interior reveal), no shared vocabulary ('access', 'presence', 'inside', 'behind'), and different transitions.

universal_viewer_check.test: Could someone who knows nothing about the creator say every line about their own life?
entry_points: The parent of a teenager who gets answers but not the kid.
The partner who keeps checking in and keeps hearing 'I'm fine'.
The person who answers every question and offers nothing, and recognises the tidy room as their own.
universal_viewer_check.changes_for_this_law: No controller or villain is addressed; 'you' is anyone who has pushed to know someone. No I, me or my. The close is a principle ('Be someone a closed door is safe around'), not a verdict on a person.

Be someone a closed door is safe around.

stills_and_motion.note: All clips start from approved stills. Motion prompts merged with the external review (clips 1-4), clip 4 kept human rather than eerie. Copied to reels/express/i2v/NDCH_036_RECEPTION.json.

motion_prompts.1: The pale oak door is already swinging slowly open in the first frame. The camera advances gently toward the doorway with a smooth, restrained forward dolly. As the door opens, more of the empty white corridor becomes visible. Natural perspective deepens gradually. The distant closed door remains stationary. Preserve the precise architecture, straight wall edges, stable floorboards, realistic hinge movement, and soft overcast daylight. Quiet photographic realism. No people.
motion_prompts.2: A continuous, exceptionally smooth forward camera movement toward the closed door across the room. The camera maintains a constant height and orientation. Natural perspective produces subtle parallax between the foreground furniture and distant wall. The chair, table, empty white cup, and blank frame remain completely stationary. The daylight remains soft and consistent. Preserve exact object proportions, architectural geometry, and realistic spatial relationships. No people.
motion_prompts.3: The camera advances slowly through the long white corridor, maintaining precise central alignment toward the distant closed door. Repeating tables, chairs, and empty cups pass gradually through the frame with natural perspective and subtle parallax. All objects remain stationary. The doors along the right wall remain unchanged. The forward movement becomes almost imperceptibly slower near the end, without stopping completely. Preserve consistent corridor dimensions, architectural geometry, object spacing, and soft daylight. No people.
motion_prompts.4: Perfectly locked camera. The closed door, brass latch, surrounding wall, and floorboards remain completely motionless. A narrow band of soft daylight is visible beneath the door. Within that band, a diffuse grey interruption gradually enters from the left, moving naturally across the illuminated floor until it settles near the center, as if someone on the other side has quietly stepped close and is standing still. It remains subtle, soft-edged, and physically plausible. Once it stops, the entire image becomes still. The door never opens. No visible person, no additional objects, no lighting change.
motion_prompts.5: Fallback only; the planned close is clip 1's first seconds played in reverse. Locked camera on the original pale oak doorway composition. The partly open door drifts a few centimetres toward closed and eases to a stop. The distant corridor door remains closed. Preserve the original architecture, door proportions, floorboards, and soft overcast daylight. No people.
